requirements.text: To keep Galaxy Buds auto switch trustworthy on Linux, the business must deliver a daemon that survives suspend/resume, Bluetooth power toggles, service restarts, and malformed BLE traffic without panicking or wedging.
To grow the user base onto the Steam Deck, the business must support installing and running seuil on stock SteamOS without disabling the immutable rootfs or installing a compiler toolchain.
To make faults diagnosable without log archaeology, the business must ship a one-command diagnostic with stable exit codes and a blocking/advisory split.
To protect user trust in Samsung account security, the business must preserve credential integrity across writes, restarts, and refresh cycles and never expose key material.
To make handoffs deterministic, the business must prevent ping-pong switching and mid-game audio hijacks driven by silent or spurious streams.

The Steam Deck user shall be able to install seuil from a prebuilt release artifact into their home directory without a compiler toolchain and have the service start and stay started across Gaming Mode and Desktop Mode switches.

The user shall be able to run one diagnostic command that reports each runtime dependency and service state, separates blocking from advisory problems, and states what to do next, including that first-run setup belongs in Desktop Mode.
The desktop user shall experience handoffs that do not flip rapidly between the phone and Linux and never lose the media link mid-handoff.

The gamer shall have the Buds stay with the current host unless real, audible media or game audio is playing; silent tabs, muted players, UI sounds, and voice-chat streams shall not trigger a media handoff, and an active call shall be honored as a call.
The user shall have a daemon that recovers by itself after suspend/resume, Bluetooth power toggles, and bluetoothd or PipeWire restarts, without a wedged or half-dead state.
The user shall trust that Samsung account credentials never appear in terminal output or logs and are never silently replaced after a partial failure.
The maintainer shall be able to run the full verification suite and receive a definitive pass or fail with zero warnings, plus tests that encode the settled timing and parsing boundaries.
seuil doctor SHALL run every check, print one line per check, exit 0 when all pass, 1 when any blocking check fails, and 2 on an internal error.

scenarios.name: Healthy system
scenarios.given: BlueZ reachable, adapter powered, PipeWire socket present, valid credentials, and a parsed advertisement carrying a CoC PSM
scenarios.then: the command prints one line per check, every line reports pass, and the exit code is 0

scenarios.name: Credentials absent is blocking
scenarios.given: no ~/.config/seuil/credentials.json
scenarios.then: the credentials check prints a blocking failure that names the Desktop Mode setup path AND the exit code is 1

scenarios.name: PSM reported as observed
scenarios.given: the latest advertisement carries PSM 0x0081 (129)
scenarios.then: the PSM line reports the observed 0x0081 and notes 128 as the default constant AND the line does not fail merely because the value differs from the default

scenarios.name: PSM check fails on connect failure
scenarios.given: the observed PSM whose CoC connect fails
scenarios.then: the PSM check fails naming the connect failure AND the exit code is 1

scenarios.name: Internal error
scenarios.given: the doctor's own machinery fails, for example an unrecoverable I/O error in its check runner
scenarios.then: the command prints an internal-error line naming the failing subsystem and exits 2

requirements.text: The installer SHALL provide a prebuilt path (install.sh --from-release) that downloads the release artifact into ~/.local/bin without invoking any compiler or package manager.

scenarios.name: Fresh Deck install
scenarios.given: a stock SteamOS Deck with network access and no Rust toolchain
scenarios.then: the binary lands at ~/.local/bin/seuil, is executable, and no compiler or package manager ran

scenarios.name: Download failure
scenarios.given: the release URL is unreachable or the checksum does not match
scenarios.then: the installer exits non-zero with a clear message and leaves no partial executable in ~/.local/bin

requirements.text: The user service SHALL stay started across a Gaming Mode to Desktop Mode session change and SHALL start on a pure Gaming Mode boot, waiting for Bluetooth readiness instead of exiting when BlueZ is not yet up.

scenarios.name: Mode round trip
scenarios.given: the service is active in Gaming Mode
scenarios.when: the user switches to Desktop Mode and later back to Gaming Mode
scenarios.then: the service remains active throughout or restarts itself within its unit policy, and the daemon is functional after the switch

scenarios.name: Bluetooth not ready at login
scenarios.given: the user manager starts the unit before bluetoothd is ready
scenarios.when: the daemon starts and the adapter is not yet powered
scenarios.then: the daemon waits with backoff instead of exiting, and proceeds once BlueZ is reachable

requirements.text: Missing optional runtime tools SHALL degrade only the matching feature with a clear persistent warning, and a failing tool invocation SHALL be distinguished from a missing service record.

scenarios.name: sdptool missing
scenarios.given: SteamOS, whose bluez-utils ships no sdptool
scenarios.then: startup completes, the SDP-dependent step is skipped, and a warning names sdptool as absent

scenarios.name: sdptool fails, service record exists
scenarios.given: sdptool present but its local SDP query exits non-zero because bluetoothd runs without the compatibility flag
scenarios.when: the daemon runs the SDP step
scenarios.then: the warning names the compatibility requirement rather than reporting the service record as absent

scenarios.name: Audio probe tools missing
scenarios.given: pactl or playerctl not installed
scenarios.when: the daemon runs and the user runs doctor
scenarios.then: both report that audio activity detection is degraded or disabled for that source

requirements.text: Setup SHALL print the optional BlueZ experimental drop-in content and the exact privileged command that installs it, SHALL write /etc only behind an explicit flag, and SHALL include the SteamOS /etc allowlist caveat in the printed text.

scenarios.name: Default run prints only
scenarios.given: setup runs without the explicit flag
scenarios.then: setup prints the override.conf content and the exact sudo install command, writes nothing under /etc, and notes that SteamOS keeps /etc files only via its migration allowlist

scenarios.name: Explicit flag writes
scenarios.given: the user passes the explicit flag
scenarios.then: the privileged command executes, and a later doctor run reports the experimental flag state

requirements.text: The release pipeline SHALL produce an x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu artifact built on a Debian 11 (glibc 2.31) baseline with rustls so no OpenSSL links, verified to run on glibc 2.31 or newer.

scenarios.name: Pipeline verification passes
scenarios.given: the release workflow builds the artifact in its Debian 11 baseline container
scenarios.then: it lists only basic system libraries compatible with glibc 2.31, no OpenSSL, and the job succeeds

scenarios.name: Linkage check fails
scenarios.given: a dependency change pulls in a library newer than the baseline
scenarios.then: the release job fails rather than shipping an artifact that will not load on SteamOS

requirements.text: The README SHALL document the Steam Deck install path and the sprint SHALL record the SteamOS install architecture in a numbered decision record under docs/decisions/.

scenarios.name: Reader follows the README
scenarios.given: a fresh Deck and the README
scenarios.when: the reader follows the Steam Deck section
scenarios.then: they reach a doctor-verified running service without leaving $HOME and know first-run setup belongs in Desktop Mode

scenarios.name: Decision recorded
scenarios.given: the sprint completes
scenarios.when: a contributor looks for the install layout and drop-in rationale
scenarios.then: the numbered decision record states the settled choices with their rationale

scenarios.name: Documentation missing
scenarios.given: the sprint's changes landed
scenarios.when: the README's Steam Deck section or the numbered decision record under docs/decisions/ is absent
scenarios.then: the requirement fails acceptance with the missing artifact named

requirements.text: The manufacturer-data parser SHALL accept payloads whose format byte validates at either offset 2 or offset 3, SHALL reject only when both readings fail, and SHALL survive truncated or malformed records without panicking and without discarding valid records elsewhere in the buffer.

scenarios.name: Offset-3 reading accepted
scenarios.given: manufacturer data 02 18 00 01 00 80 07 48 00 48 00 (11 bytes; format byte 0x01 at offset 3, context bytes at offsets 4 to 8, fallback audio byte at 9, per docs/PROTOCOL_SPEC.md sections 2.2, 2.5, and 2.6)
scenarios.then: the payload decodes to a device context with CoC PSM 0x0080 (128), DS 0x07, NS 0x48, and F 0x00 AND the audio state is Streaming (fallback anchor byte 9 = 0x48)

scenarios.name: Offset-2 reading accepted
scenarios.given: the same logical payload with the format byte at offset 2: 02 18 01 00 00 80 07 48 00 48 00 (the original-findings reading recorded in docs/PROTOCOL_SPEC.md section 2.8)
scenarios.then: the payload decodes to the same device context (CoC PSM 0x0080, DS 0x07, NS 0x48, F 0x00) and audio state Streaming as the offset-3 reading, rather than being rejected

scenarios.name: Recoverable malformed record skipped
scenarios.given: a buffer whose first LTV record is malformed without overrunning the buffer end (for example a zero-length record) and whose later records include a valid type 1 record
scenarios.then: the walk skips the malformed record and still parses the later valid type 1 record, with no panic

scenarios.name: Overrunning record ends the walk safely
scenarios.given: a record whose declared length overruns the buffer end
scenarios.then: the walk ends gracefully with no panic AND any type 1 record already decoded before the overrun remains in the parse result

scenarios.name: Garbage payload
scenarios.given: random bytes prefixed with a plausible Samsung header
scenarios.then: parsing returns rejection without panicking

scenarios.name: Account-bound audio-state anchor
scenarios.given: an account-bound advertisement whose type 1 record carries NS 0x48 at the record-local anchor (body_start + 3, docs/PROTOCOL_SPEC.md section 2.5)
scenarios.then: the audio state is Streaming AND the same record with NS 0x08 parses Idle AND the same record with NS 0x00 parses Disconnected

scenarios.name: Fallback audio-state anchor
scenarios.given: an unbound advertisement whose account-bound parse is unavailable, with manufacturer-data byte 9 equal to 0x48 (masked 0xF8, docs/PROTOCOL_SPEC.md sections 2.5 and 2.6)
scenarios.then: the audio state is Streaming AND byte 9 equal to 0x08 parses Idle AND byte 9 equal to 0x18 parses Disconnected

requirements.text: On suspend (logind PrepareForSleep true) and on adapter power-off, the daemon SHALL tear down CoC channels and stop scanning and advertising; on wake or power-on it SHALL re-initialize each session exactly once, with no duplicate advertisements, leaked tasks, or stale channel entries.

scenarios.name: Suspend and wake
scenarios.given: the daemon running with one advertisement, one discovery session, and one CoC channel
scenarios.when: the system suspends and later wakes
scenarios.then: teardown closed the channel and stopped scan and advertising, and after wake exactly one advertisement, one discovery session, and one redial attempt exist

scenarios.name: Adapter power toggle
scenarios.given: the daemon running
scenarios.when: the adapter powers off and on again
scenarios.then: the daemon reaches the same clean state as after a wake, without needing a service restart

scenarios.name: Rapid sleep and wake flapping
scenarios.given: repeated quick suspend and wake cycles
scenarios.then: the daemon converges to exactly one active advertisement and one discovery session, with no leaked tasks

requirements.text: The daemon SHALL enforce a 10 s minimum dwell between handoff requests and an exponential CoC connect backoff starting at 1 s and capped at 60 s, both configurable in config.toml with those defaults.

scenarios.name: Second request inside the dwell
scenarios.given: a handoff request sent less than 10 s ago
scenarios.then: the new request is suppressed and logged as dwell-blocked

scenarios.name: Request after the dwell
scenarios.given: the last handoff request was 10 s ago or more
scenarios.then: the request proceeds

scenarios.name: Backoff sequence on repeated connect failures
scenarios.given: the phone is unreachable
scenarios.then: retry delays follow 1, 2, 4, and so on, capped at 60 s

scenarios.name: Custom configuration honored
scenarios.given: config.toml sets a different dwell or backoff
scenarios.then: the configured values are used

requirements.text: The daemon SHALL pair and dial only advertisements from the configured phone address and SHALL verify inbound advertisement checksums against the account fingerprint before acting on them.

scenarios.name: Spoofed advertisement ignored
scenarios.given: a 0x0075 advertisement with a type 1 record from an address other than the configured phone
scenarios.then: no pairing and no dial occur, and a warning names the rejected address

scenarios.name: Bad checksum ignored
scenarios.given: an advertisement from the configured phone whose checksum does not match the account fingerprint
scenarios.then: the payload is not acted on

scenarios.name: Valid advertisement acted on
scenarios.given: a type 1 advertisement from the configured phone whose checksum matches the account fingerprint
scenarios.then: pairing and dial proceed under the timing requirements

requirements.text: Background event loops SHALL handle address-parse and crypto-size failures as errors, bound keepalive and frame reads with timeouts configurable in config.toml (default 10 s each), and cap per-peer bookkeeping maps at a configurable limit (config.toml, default 256 entries).

scenarios.name: Malformed address string
scenarios.given: an address string that fails to parse reaches an event handler
scenarios.then: the failure is logged as an error and the loop and its task continue

scenarios.name: Stalled peer
scenarios.given: a CoC peer stops responding mid-frame
scenarios.when: the read timeout expires at its configured limit (default 10 s)
scenarios.then: the channel tears down cleanly and the map entry is removed

scenarios.name: Crypto-size failure contained
scenarios.given: a crypto operation receives a wrong-size key or nonce
scenarios.then: the failure is logged as an error and the loop continues without panicking

scenarios.name: Keepalive timeout tears down
scenarios.given: a CoC peer that stops acknowledging keepalive writes
scenarios.when: the keepalive timeout expires at its configured limit (default 10 s)
scenarios.then: the channel tears down cleanly and its map entry is removed

scenarios.name: Rotating spoofed addresses
scenarios.given: hours of advertisements from rotating random addresses
scenarios.then: their size never exceeds the per-peer bookkeeping cap configured in config.toml, defaulting to 256 entries

requirements.text: The daemon SHALL route auto switch traffic per the settled transport split: phone-directed commands over the BLE L2CAP CoC and Buds opcodes (SET_SEAMLESS_CONNECTION and its acknowledgement) over RFCOMM SPP, with the Buds SPP frame parser rejecting short or malformed frames without panicking.

scenarios.name: Phone-directed commands ride the CoC
scenarios.given: the CoC established by the account handshake
scenarios.when: a BUDS_SWITCH request or response, ready event, or get-device-state flows
scenarios.then: it travels on the BLE CoC channel AND no phone-directed command travels over SPP

scenarios.name: Seamless handoff delivered
scenarios.given: a yield to the phone completes
scenarios.then: SET_SEAMLESS_CONNECTION reaches the Buds over SPP and the acknowledgement is processed

scenarios.name: Malformed SPP frame
scenarios.given: an SPP frame with a declared size under 2 or a truncated body
scenarios.then: the frame is dropped with a warning and the session continues without panic

requirements.text: The daemon SHALL prevent concurrency faults with observable outcomes: a closed channel leaves no entry that blocks future dials to that peer, one peer's blocked channel does not stall other peers, and a hung connect attempt does not accumulate duplicates.

scenarios.name: Closed channel does not block redial
scenarios.given: a dial whose channel closes immediately
scenarios.when: the same peer is dialed again
scenarios.then: the new dial proceeds, not blocked by the old one's state

scenarios.name: Backpressure does not stall unrelated peers
scenarios.given: one peer's channel blocked or saturated
scenarios.then: the other peer is served

scenarios.name: Hung attempt does not duplicate
scenarios.given: a first connect attempt that has not completed
scenarios.then: no duplicate attempt runs concurrently AND a later retry proceeds once the first attempt resolves or times out

requirements.text: Discovery restarts SHALL stop the previous session before reapplying filters, a rejected discovery filter SHALL produce a visible warning, and the advertiser SHALL retry registration failures with backoff instead of exiting.

scenarios.name: Adapter loss and return
scenarios.given: the adapter disappears and comes back
scenarios.then: exactly one discovery session is active afterward

scenarios.name: Previous session stopped first
scenarios.given: a discovery session running when the scan loop restarts
scenarios.when: the restart re-applies the discovery filter and opens a new stream
scenarios.then: the previous session was stopped before the filter was re-applied AND exactly one discovery session is active

scenarios.name: Advertisement registration collision
scenarios.given: an advertisement re-registration that fails because the previous one is still unregistering
scenarios.then: it retries with backoff and advertising continues for the process lifetime

scenarios.name: Filter rejection surfaced
scenarios.given: BlueZ rejects the discovery filter
scenarios.then: a warning names the rejection instead of silently proceeding

requirements.text: The media monitor SHALL treat a stream as active only while it is RUNNING and its peak stays above -60 dBFS across a 200 ms window, SHALL exclude capture-side and communication-class streams, and SHALL expose the threshold and window as config.toml keys with those defaults.

scenarios.name: Silent tab is not activity
scenarios.given: a browser tab holding a RUNNING but digitally silent stream
scenarios.then: the stream is not active and no handoff request fires

scenarios.name: Real game audio is activity
scenarios.given: game audio playing above the threshold
scenarios.when: the peak stays above -60 dBFS across the 200 ms window
scenarios.then: the stream is active and one media-reason request fires

scenarios.name: Communication stream excluded
scenarios.given: a voice-chat stream classified as communication or capture
scenarios.then: it does not count as media activity

scenarios.name: Thresholds configurable
scenarios.given: config.toml sets a different threshold or window
scenarios.then: the configured values are used

requirements.text: An active HFP call SHALL block media-reason handoffs, call-reason switching SHALL remain allowed during HFP, and the call guard SHALL be scoped to call-reason responses rather than cleared by any response.

scenarios.name: Media trigger during a call
scenarios.given: an active HFP call on the Buds
scenarios.then: the media-reason handoff is suppressed

scenarios.name: Call-reason switching during HFP
scenarios.given: an active HFP call
scenarios.then: it proceeds

scenarios.name: Lost call response does not lock media
scenarios.given: a call-reason response that never arrives
scenarios.then: media handoffs are not blocked by a blanket timed lock

requirements.text: Probe or service failures SHALL NOT fabricate activity edges: a failed probe SHALL hold the last known state rather than emitting a stop followed by a start, probes SHALL be timeout-bounded, and the monitor task SHALL be supervised so its death is visible and recoverable.

scenarios.name: Probe tool absent
scenarios.given: pactl missing from the system
scenarios.then: one persistent warning is logged, the last known activity state is held, and no stop/start edge pair is emitted

scenarios.name: Probe hangs
scenarios.given: a probe subprocess that never returns
scenarios.then: the tick completes and later ticks continue

scenarios.name: Monitor task dies
scenarios.given: the media monitor task exits or panics
scenarios.then: the task is restarted and an error is logged

scenarios.name: PipeWire restart recovery
scenarios.given: the PipeWire daemon restarting while the daemon runs
scenarios.when: the monitor reconnects after the restart
scenarios.then: activity evaluation resumes without a fabricated edge pair

requirements.text: On a release request the daemon SHALL verify the pause succeeded and complete profile teardown before answering the phone, and on a granted switch it SHALL retry the A2DP connect; a call-reason response SHALL NOT trigger an A2DP pull.

scenarios.name: Pause failure is reported
scenarios.given: MPRIS pause fails during a release
scenarios.then: the reply to the phone reflects the failure rather than claiming success

scenarios.name: Teardown before reply
scenarios.given: a release with A2DP and HFP links up
scenarios.then: the profile disconnects have completed or their failure is reported in the reply's result path

scenarios.name: A2DP pull retries
scenarios.given: a granted media switch whose first A2DP connect fails or is slow
scenarios.then: bounded retries occur before giving up with a warning

scenarios.name: Call-reason grant leaves media alone
scenarios.given: the phone grants a call-reason switch
scenarios.then: no A2DP pull is initiated

requirements.text: A missing, unreadable, or wrong-length credentials.key SHALL fail credential loading with a specific error and no silent regeneration, and credential writes SHALL be atomic, durable across a crash, and resilient to stale temp files.

scenarios.name: Key deleted, envelope remains
scenarios.given: credentials.json present and credentials.key deleted
scenarios.then: loading fails with an error naming the key file, and no new key is written

scenarios.name: Key unreadable
scenarios.given: credentials.key with permissions or ownership that deny reading
scenarios.then: loading fails naming the key file AND no new key is written

scenarios.name: Key wrong length
scenarios.given: credentials.key containing a length other than 32 bytes
scenarios.then: loading fails naming the length mismatch AND no new key is written

scenarios.name: Crash mid-save
scenarios.given: a save interrupted by a crash or power loss
scenarios.then: the previous envelope is intact and decryptable

scenarios.name: Stale temp file
scenarios.given: a leftover temp file from a crashed save
scenarios.then: the save succeeds without manual cleanup

requirements.text: The daemon and setup SHALL NOT print account keys or tokens to stdout or logs, and debug formatting of credential structures SHALL redact secret fields.

scenarios.name: Auth run prints no key material
scenarios.given: a successful account authentication or refresh
scenarios.then: no account key, token, or private key material appears in stdout or logs

scenarios.name: Debug formatting redacted
scenarios.given: a credential structure printed with debug formatting
scenarios.then: secret fields are redacted

requirements.text: config.toml and the systemd unit SHALL be written atomically, the config directory SHALL carry owner-only permissions, and an invalid config.toml SHALL abort startup with the parse error instead of silently using defaults.

scenarios.name: Crash during config save
scenarios.given: a config write interrupted by a crash
scenarios.when: setup or the daemon next reads the file
scenarios.then: the previous content is intact

scenarios.name: Interrupted unit write
scenarios.given: a systemd unit write interrupted by a crash
scenarios.when: setup next reads the unit file
scenarios.then: the previous unit content is intact

scenarios.name: TOML typo aborts
scenarios.given: a config.toml with a syntax error
scenarios.then: startup aborts with an error naming the file and the parse failure

scenarios.name: Directory permissions
scenarios.given: a fresh install
scenarios.then: the directory is owner-only (0700) even when a parent defaults to group or world readable

requirements.text: The daemon SHALL refresh expiring tokens at runtime, re-enroll when the handshake indicates invalid credentials with bounded retries and a user-visible escalation, re-acquire its Bluetooth session after a bluetoothd restart, and back off pairing failures.

scenarios.name: Token refresh at runtime
scenarios.given: a service token whose expiry enters the 120-second refresh margin while the daemon runs
scenarios.then: the token is refreshed and persisted without user action AND a token whose expiry lies outside the margin does not trigger a refresh

scenarios.name: Certificate rotation escalates
scenarios.given: the stored certificate rejected by the handshake
scenarios.then: a clear escalation tells the user to rerun setup instead of retrying silently forever

scenarios.name: bluetoothd restart recovery
scenarios.given: bluetoothd restarted
scenarios.when: the daemon notices the dead session
scenarios.then: it re-acquires the adapter and session with backoff and resumes scanning and advertising

scenarios.name: Pairing failures back off
scenarios.given: repeated pairing failures, for example a permissions problem
scenarios.then: delays grow rather than retrying flatly, and the failure is visible

requirements.text: The test suite SHALL cover malformed LTV and L2CAP frames under both format-byte readings, the audio-state anchor on short and long advertisements, the dwell and backoff boundaries, sleep/wake state resets, the active-audio filter rule, and the doctor exit contract, and every existing test SHALL keep passing.

scenarios.name: Settled boundaries covered
scenarios.given: the settled decisions
scenarios.then: each boundary has a test: malformed LTV frames and malformed L2CAP frames under both format-byte readings, the audio-state anchor on short and long advertisements, the 10 s dwell edge, the 1 s and 60 s backoff edges, sleep/wake state convergence, the peak-window rule, and doctor exit codes

scenarios.name: Regression held
scenarios.given: the existing test suite
scenarios.then: every existing test still passes

scenarios.name: Boundary uncovered
scenarios.given: a settled boundary with no citing test
scenarios.then: the requirement fails acceptance naming the uncovered boundary

requirements.text: The sprint SHALL be verified by cargo check, cargo clippy with warnings denied, cargo test, and a release build, all passing; the live phone gate is reported pending as a separate pre-merge criterion.

scenarios.name: All gates green
scenarios.given: the implementation complete
scenarios.then: cargo check, clippy with -D warnings, cargo test, and the release build all exit 0 with zero warnings

scenarios.name: A gate fails
scenarios.given: any gate failing or warning
scenarios.then: the producing step fixes it before the sprint is called complete, and the live phone gate is reported as pending, not silently passed

requirements.text: The media monitor SHALL settle an activity-state change within 1 s of the underlying stream change at default settings.
The daemon SHALL keep account keys, tokens, and certificates out of stdout, logs, and debug output in every code path.
The daemon SHALL expose no panic path reachable from malformed BLE, L2CAP, or SPP input.
The daemon SHALL re-establish scanning, advertising, and its Bluetooth session within 60 s of bluetoothd becoming reachable again after a restart.
Doctor output SHALL be one line per check, each naming the check, its result, and for failures the next action.

All user-installed state SHALL live under $HOME at the settled paths: binary at ~/.local/bin, config and credentials at ~/.config/seuil/, user unit at ~/.config/systemd/user/; any suggested /etc change documents the SteamOS allowlist caveat; the portable artifact runs on glibc 2.31 or newer with no OpenSSL linkage.
cargo clippy on all targets with warnings denied SHALL pass with zero warnings.
